vocabulary.meaning_en: it is important for me; I will get a benefit if I do it
vocabulary.note_en: Followed by the base verb: need to go.
vocabulary.example: I need to drink more water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: it is necessary; there will be a problem if I don't do it
vocabulary.example: I have to pay my bills today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: it is necessary (often a rule or strong feeling)
vocabulary.example: You must wear a seat belt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you must have or do
something you must do because of a rule, a duty or a promise
a result of an action, often a bad one
vocabulary.example: If you are late, the consequence is a fine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the feeling that something must be done quickly

vocabulary.example: Have means possess: I have a book.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you want to reach or get
vocabulary.example: My goal is to speak English well.
The word "to" shows direction: go to school.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money people must pay to the government
a room with a toilet (Canadian English)
vocabulary.note_ar: في بريطانيا toilet وفي أمريكا restroom/bathroom

vocabulary.meaning_en: to lose a chance to get something good
vocabulary.example: Come early, or you will miss out.

fine_lines.title: need to vs have to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى متقارب، لكن need to تركّز على الفائدة لي (سأكون أفضل إذا فعلت)، أما have to فتركّز على العاقبة (ستحدث مشكلة إذا لم أفعل). تذكّر: need = me (فائدة لي).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both are similar, but need to thinks about the benefit for me (I will feel better), and have to thinks about the consequence (there will be a problem if I don't). Remember: "need" rhymes with "me" (good for me).

examples.sentence: I need to rest. I will feel better.
I have to finish this report today, or my boss will be angry.

fine_lines.title: teacher's view vs student's view
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعلم يقول للطالب: You have to do your homework (عليك واجب وستحدث عاقبة). والطالب يقول: I need to do my homework (لمصلحتي). الاثنان صحيحان من زاويتين مختلفتين.
fine_lines.explanation_en: The teacher says "You have to do your homework" (an obligation with a consequence). The student says "I need to do my homework" (for my benefit). Both are correct, from two points of view.

examples.sentence: You have to do your homework.
I need to do my homework to improve.

expressions.meaning_en: I must leave now; I don't have a choice.
expressions.example: Sorry, I have to go. My bus is here.

expressions.meaning_en: It is a good idea for me to leave now.
expressions.example: It's late. I need to go and sleep.

expressions.phrase: You need to stop right now.
expressions.example: You are very tired. You need to stop right now.

expressions.meaning_en: It is not necessary for me.
expressions.example: It's Friday. I don't have to work.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking how two things are not the same.
expressions.example: Need to and have to: what's the difference?

grammar.title: Have to + base verb (obligation and consequence)
grammar.explanation_ar: have to + المصدر تعني أنك مضطر لفعل شيء، وإن لم تفعله ستحدث عاقبة. have = تملك، to = اتجاه/هدف. لذلك نشعر بالاستعجال. مع he/she/it نقول has to.
grammar.explanation_en: have to + base verb means you must do something, or there will be a consequence. Have = possess, to = goal/direction. People feel urgency. With he/she/it use has to.
examples: I have to go to the bank before it closes.
She has to pay her taxes this month.
We have to leave now, or we will miss the train.

grammar.title: Need to + base verb (benefit for me)
grammar.explanation_ar: need to + المصدر: الأمر مهم لي وأحصل منه على فائدة، والاستعجال أقل. مع he/she/it نقول needs to.
grammar.explanation_en: need to + base verb: it is important to me and I get a benefit; less urgency. With he/she/it use needs to.

grammar.title: Negatives and questions
grammar.explanation_ar: النفي: don't/doesn't have to (غير ضروري)، don't/doesn't need to (غير ضروري). السؤال: Do you have to...? / Do you need to...?
grammar.explanation_en: Negative: don't/doesn't have to (not necessary), don't/doesn't need to (not necessary). Question: Do you have to...? / Do you need to...?
examples: I don't have to work on Friday.
You don't need to bring anything.
Do you have to go now?

questions.question: Which one focuses on the benefit for me?
questions.explanation_en: Need to = a benefit for me.

questions.question: "I have to go to the bank now, or it will close." Why "have to"?
questions.explanation_en: There is a consequence: the bank will close.

questions.question: She ___ finish her work before five.
What does "obligation" mean?
questions.explanation_en: An obligation is something you must do.

questions.question: It's Saturday. I ___ go to work.
questions.explanation_en: don't have to = it is not necessary.

questions.question: What does "consequence" mean?
questions.explanation_en: A consequence is a result of an action.

questions.question: A teacher says to a student: "You ___ do your homework."
questions.explanation_ar: المعلم يفرض واجبًا وله عاقبة: have to.
questions.explanation_en: The teacher gives an obligation with a consequence: have to.

questions.question: In "have to", what does "to" show?
questions.explanation_ar: to تدل على الهدف أو الاتجاه.

questions.question: ___ you have to work tomorrow?
questions.explanation_ar: السؤال مع have to يكون بـ Do.
questions.explanation_en: Questions with have to use Do.
